actions.heading: Recommended actions, in order
paragraphs: First, record the refusal and keep v3 unserved, because Luhya at {F002}% is below the {F003}% floor. Second, diagnose the Kikamba fall from {F006}% to {F007}% and the Gikuyu fall from {F008}% to {F009}% before changing the recipe, so the next version fixes a known cause.

Third, run a dedicated check on the speaker probe finding, since it is a privacy concern and the record holds no figure for it. Fourth, write the next acceptance with a per-stratum no-regression floor, and commission fresh, independently labelled and sealed final material.

chapter1.heading: The decision and what it was measured against
paragraphs: The decision was a refusal against the signed acceptance. The target stratum, Luhya, recorded {F002}% against a floor of {F003}%. The refusal does not rest on Luhya alone. Every other measured stratum regressed from its earlier score.

Ekegusii fell from {F004}% to {F005}%, Kikamba from {F006}% to {F007}%, Gikuyu from {F008}% to {F009}%, Kalenjin from {F010}% to {F011}%, luo from {F012}% to {F036}% and Kiswahili from {F014}% to {F015}%. The speaker probe on the served output also scored above chance.

chapter2.heading: Measurements by stratum
paragraphs: Ekegusii is the only stratum above its {F041}% floor, at {F040}%, with {F042}% abstained. Kikamba scored {F043}% with {F045}% abstained. Gikuyu scored {F046}% with {F048}% abstained, the highest abstention rate on the record.

Kalenjin scored {F049}% with {F051}% abstained. Luo scored {F052}% with {F054}% abstained. Luhya scored {F002}% with {F057}% abstained, and Kiswahili scored {F058}% with {F060}% abstained. The record does not say whether accuracy is calculated over answered items only, so the abstention rates are context, not an adjustment.

chapter3.heading: Compute
paragraphs: The run took {F022} minutes on the akki-vm host, on device {F023}, with peak memory of {F024} GB. This is a modest footprint, and nothing in the record suggests that compute limited the result.
The record holds no cap figure that can be cited, so the comparison with the signed cap cannot be made here. The trained artefact stays on the compute host, which any follow-up test will need to use.

chapter4.heading: What the owner should do with this model
paragraphs: Do not serve v3. The target stratum is below its floor at {F002}% against {F003}%, and serving would also expose users in other languages to lower scores than before. Ekegusii at {F005}% is nearest its floor; Kikamba at {F007}% and Gikuyu at {F009}% are furthest from theirs.

The record does not explain why the regressions occurred, so the next version should begin with a diagnosis. Further selection against these results would also weaken any later acceptance claim, because they have been inspected.

risks.heading: What the record cannot yet establish
paragraphs: This record covers one historical run only. It does not establish performance outside the measured strata, which would need an independently designed evaluation. It cannot support independent final acceptance, because the results have been inspected; fresh, independently labelled and sealed material would be needed.

Nor does it give a complete lineage from objective to production, because no new production plan is linked to this run. An explicitly compiled, evidence-linked objective would close that gap, and it should not be backdated.

summary: The Luhya reinforcement run for audio language model v3 was refused against its signed acceptance. Luhya scored {F002}% against a floor of {F003}%, so the stratum it was meant to improve did not pass. Six other strata scored below their earlier results, and a speaker probe on the served output was above chance.

The sharpest regressions were Kikamba, from {F006}% to {F007}%, and Gikuyu, from {F008}% to {F009}%. Ekegusii is the only stratum above the floor, at {F005}%. The recommendation is not to serve v3, to find the cause of the regressions, and to open a next version with per-stratum guards, a speaker-leakage check and fresh sealed evaluation material.
